title: Can We Trust AI Too Much? A Robot Expert Has Questions
summary:
Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing how we work, learn and live. Geoff Bennett of the News Hour talked with Dr. Ayanna Howard about using it well. Howard is a robotics expert who started her career at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory and is now the president of Spelman College.

Howard has spent over 30 years building AI and robots. She studies overtrust — trusting machines more than we should. We ask AI for help because we want it to know more than we do, she says, so it can feel like a teacher, and we believe it even when it is wrong.

She worries about how AI changes the way kids learn. Students use it daily, but teachers have not worked out how to teach kids to use it safely — or when not to use it at all. Like a parent showing a child how to use a new gadget, she says, we need to guide kids with AI too.

Used well, AI can help us think better, Howard says. It will also change many jobs, though not replace all of them.
why_it_matters: If you use AI for homework or learning, knowing when to trust it and when to check it yourself helps you really learn instead of just copying answers that might be wrong.

background_read: Artificial intelligence, or AI, is a kind of computer program that can learn from information and help people with tasks like answering questions and solving problems.
People created AI to make work and learning faster and easier, and it is now part of many tools we use every day.
Dr. Ayanna Howard builds AI and robots, and she studies what happens when people trust machines more than they should.
Article_Structure: WHO: Dr. Ayanna Howard, a robotics expert, and Geoff Bennett of the News Hour
WHAT: Howard talks about overtrust, trusting AI more than we should, and how kids should learn to use AI safely
WHERE: NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, where Howard began her career, and Spelman College, where she works now
WHY: Because AI is changing how kids learn and work, and Howard wants people to use it wisely instead of trusting it blindly

perspectives.description: AI can help us think better when used well, but we should not trust it blindly, and kids need guidance to learn when to use it and when not to.
